sections.heading: Greetings by time of day
sections.body:
*Hola* (hello) works any time, with anyone. For something a little more polite, use the greeting for the time of day:

- *Buenos días* — good morning (until about noon)
- *Buenas tardes* — good afternoon (from noon until dark)
- *Buenas noches* — good evening / good night (after dark, both to greet and to say goodbye)

In Latin America it is very common to combine them: *Hola, buenos días.* Many people shorten them in casual speech to *buenas*. In Argentina and Uruguay you will often hear *buen día* in the morning.

sections.heading: How are you?
sections.body:
After the greeting, people ask how you are:

- *¿Qué tal?* — How's it going? (casual, very common)
- *¿Cómo estás?* — How are you? (to a friend, someone your age, a child)
- *¿Cómo está usted?* — How are you? (polite: to an older person, a customer, someone you don't know)

Typical answers: *Bien, gracias.* (Fine, thanks.) *Muy bien.* (Very well.) *Más o menos.* (So-so.) *Mal.* (Bad.) Then bounce the question back: *¿Y tú?* (And you?) or, politely, *¿Y usted?*

sections.heading: Saying goodbye
sections.body:
- *Adiós* — goodbye
- *Hasta luego* — see you later (the most common everyday goodbye)
- *Hasta mañana* — see you tomorrow
- *Nos vemos* — see you
- *Chao* — bye (very common in much of Latin America; also spelled *chau* in Argentina)

When you leave a shop or office, *hasta luego* or *que le vaya bien* (may it go well for you) is friendly and polite.

sections.heading: Greeting customs
sections.body: In much of Latin America, people greet friends and acquaintances with one kiss on the right cheek (women with women, and men with women); men often shake hands or hug. In shops and lifts it is normal to say *buenos días* or *buenas tardes* to everyone present — silence can seem rude.

exercises.prompt: It's 9 a.m. How do you greet your neighbor politely?
It's 10 p.m. and you're leaving a party. What do you say?
Which question would you ask an older stranger?
What does *más o menos* mean as an answer to "how are you?"
Which is the most common everyday way to say "see you later"?
Someone says *¿Qué tal?* The best reply is…

options: both to greet and to say goodbye in the evening

exercises.hint: See you later. (or see you tomorrow)

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "Good afternoon, how are you?" (formal)
Put the words in order: "Very well, thank you. And you?" (formal)
